674de15a6888537b9f23127407718b32._desc:
Library staff reported that "the city's doing a lot of El Nino prep" and is discussing whether the library should remain open during major flooding or close to encourage people to stay off the roads. Staff said the city would provide direction and that the county was coordinating a broader response through a jurisdictional meeting involving police, fire, and city managers.

Asked whether the library has a generator, staff explained: "They have to get it. So that if they can get a generator, they can put it in there and hook it up and run it. But they decided not to buy one." The facility has solar panels and some backup capability, but staff said that only certain functions are backed up and that the library would not operate at full power capacity. Basic electricity and data could potentially remain available, although staff needed to confirm the details.

Staff further stated: "I have to find out a little bit more precisely cuz obviously if there's a long-term outage, there's going to probably be other people who want a generator ... too to get one over here. But I would think we might have priority as a city." The board discussed how having a generator could allow the library to remain fully operational while other parts of the city are without power, affecting its potential emergency role.

This presents a conditional opportunity for emergency generator rental or supply, delivery, and connection support if the city determines that the library should remain operational during an outage. The city had decided against purchasing a permanent generator, and no rental decision, supplier, budget, equipment specifications, or acquisition deadline was established.

a3743b4fb53d540bba3bbd768039e3eb.Title: Water Street Festival Production, Rentals and Promotion
a3743b4fb53d540bba3bbd768039e3eb._desc:
The Water Street BID board discussed additional funding to ensure that a planned Water Street event could proceed and approved a motion to take an additional $5,000 from BID financial reserves. The BID had initially committed $5,000, but the event organizer explained that this was a much bigger event than originally contemplated and that the initial amount covered planning, logistics, staff time and contractor time. The proposed event was approximately 30 days away at the time of the June 22, 2026 meeting, with council consideration expected the following day. The organizer stated that the event could not proceed as proposed without additional support and city approval.

External purchasing needs discussed included booking three bands, a stage that would allow music to continue in rain, and professional production support. The organizer described the stage as the biggest expense in the main-stage portion of the budget. Art installations and activities were also included, with some larger pieces planned for Fourth Avenue and other activities along the street or sidewalk. Stage teardown would occur immediately after the event, and the organizer expected vendors to clear the street within approximately one hour.

Sanitation requirements included five regular portable toilets and a handwashing station. A quote had already been obtained from the organizer's usual vendor, whose name is unclear in the captions, although the organizer said they might try to negotiate a lower price. Street-closure safety requirements initially called for concrete Jersey barriers, but the city agreed that dump trucks or buses could instead block the street. A potential arrangement for four buses had been identified through a board member's acquaintance; whether these would be donated entirely or require reimbursement remained to be confirmed. These arrangements may limit the remaining opportunity for barrier or vehicle rental providers.

The organizer also identified $4,000 in visitor-grant funding restricted to promotional purposes, contingent on conducting the event as proposed. The budget included advertising and promotional assets that could be purchased using those grant dollars. Discussion included social media video, producing a passport for the associated Week on Water program, distributing information to participating businesses, and coordinated promotion with another festival. The organizer said a tourism partner would match the $4,000 expenditure with $4,000 in marketing support and was awaiting confirmation that the event would proceed.

Potential vendor work therefore includes remaining entertainment bookings, stage rental and production, sanitation rental, promotional-content production, advertising and printed event materials. Some planning and contractor work was already underway, and some rental arrangements were already being explored. The additional $5,000 approved by the board is supporting event funding, not an identified contract value. Required city

714903762bdd5390b255735183969a4e.Title: Potential 2027 Independence Day Event Services Recompete
714903762bdd5390b255735183969a4e._desc:
The 2026 4th of July Event Recap for the City of San Marino indicates several areas where the City expects to make changes for next year’s Independence Day celebration at Lacy Park and along the community parade route. Staff states that event planning, led by the Recreation Division, requires a large amount of coordination between various City departments, community partners, and vendors, and that the event-day activities included the J.P. Blecksmith Memorial Run, Family Fun Zone, community parade, City Club’s Pavilion, food vendors, and fireworks show. The report also notes that attendance increased to 11,898 in 2026 and that the celebration averages around 10,000 attendees over the past five years, suggesting a substantial annual event with recurring outside vendor needs.

Most importantly for future procurement, the report identifies specific vendor-related shortcomings and planned improvements for next year. Staff wrote that the new restroom company delivered the restrooms late and the units did not match, and explicitly stated: “Next year, staff will utilize a different restroom vendor.” This strongly indicates a likely future purchase of portable restroom rental and related support services for the 2027 event. The report also states that “Securing food vendors was a challenge this year” and that next year staff will begin vendor outreach earlier, reach out to more vendors, and secure commitments farther in advance. That suggests an upcoming need for food vending participation and potentially event vendor coordination services.

In addition, staff identified operational needs that may create opportunities for contracted event support services. The City plans to expand the parade staging area by one block, revise the event layout to create a larger designated dance area in front of the stage, and refine the staging and release process with clearer spacing instructions and additional staff or volunteers to maintain parade flow. While not framed as a formal solicitation yet, these statements indicate prospective needs for event logistics support, temporary event operations services, traffic and crowd management equipment, site layout planning, portable sanitation, and possibly related technology or payment-support infrastructure given the report’s reference to Starlink, tap-to-pay, and Square systems working well.

The document concludes that staff will develop viable solutions and recommendations addressing operational, safety, and liability issues for next year’s event. That forward-looking language, combined with the explicit statement that a different restroom vendor will be used next year, makes this the clearest potential contracting lead in the packet.

087bf4b2422a58df9eb43dce2e197ec8._desc:
Officials discussed future procurement of equipment and services for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic activation sites, specifically including portable toilets and fencing. In the activation-site report, staff said they had received cost information for 'equipo, como cercos, baños ... portátiles' and were continuing to develop the operating budget and implementation details.

A councilmember specifically raised the cost of securing installations every night and during periods when events are not operating. Staff reported conversations with the Police Department, which wanted assurance that public safety would be controlled, and said there were several ways to manage security with differing costs. No security deployment model or outside security contract was finalized, but the discussion establishes a potential need for site-security services alongside temporary event equipment.

Accessibility was a significant lesson from the previous FIFA events. The Office of Major Events said accessible site design had been lacking at some locations and that outside contractors supplying toilets and similar facilities did not sufficiently understand accessibility requirements. The office intends to focus on this issue for 2028 and asked municipal departments to do the same. Site planning must also address safe entrance and exit, crowd circulation, public transportation access, and public safety.

Officials warned that the City would compete with corporations and other government entities for equipment in 2028, particularly portable toilets, and emphasized early procurement and cost control. The broader activation procurement process is expected to proceed through RFP work in 2027. Final equipment quantities, security requirements, site counts, operating schedules, and contract packaging remain unresolved.

The project is being managed by Capital Engineering. Staff expects an invitation for bid, described as a hard bid with a bid schedule matching the construction drawings. The lowest responsible bidder would be brought to City Council for contract award, provided the bid is within budget. Staff said they hope to work with the project manager soon on issuing the bid and obtaining a general contractor to perform the work.

The project will combine two existing restroom units off the alley between Uptown Billiards and the Hopi Trust building into one room, increasing the total number of toilets from two to three. The proposed configuration includes one ADA-accessible restroom partition with an adult changing station required by Arizona law, two smaller restroom partitions, one handwashing sink, and a custodial closet. The closet will provide a mop or janitorial sink and storage for cleaning supplies, paper products, and soap. The Downtown Business Alliance clean team currently cleans the restrooms and will continue cleaning the reconstructed facility; staff did not describe a new cleaning procurement.

The restrooms will not be gender specific. An overhead garage-style door will close and secure the facility when it is not open to the public. The design calls for restroom partitions with a nine-inch gap at the bottom and a height of six feet eight inches beneath a nine-foot ceiling. Staff described these features as intended to discourage prolonged occupancy while retaining privacy for restroom use.

Some specifications remain under discussion with the architect, particularly a red-light/green-light occupancy indication system operated by the stall latches. Staff prefers a cost-effective ceiling-mounted indicator rather than expensive European partitions incorporating illuminated strips. The reference to '$500,000 worth of partitions' was an illustration of an unacceptable expense, not the project estimate.

The entire project budget is $250,000 for design and construction, with Capital Engineering project-management costs also drawing on that amount. Some funding has already been consumed by design and related work, so the amount available for the construction contract is less than $250,000. Staff is awaiting actual bids to establish construction costs.

During an estimated four-to-six-month construction period, temporary portable restroom units will be needed at Heritage Square to replace the existing facilities. Their location and arrangement have not yet been determined. This creates a related potential requirement for portable restroom rental and servicing, either within the construction scope or separately. 1eb5060308305b5a8b7604c9255004d5.Title: Pear Tree Concession Conversion to Accessible Family Restrooms
1eb5060308305b5a8b7604c9255004d5._desc:
Staff proposed repurposing at least part of the Pear Tree concession area into one or more family restrooms. Existing ADA renovations left only one toilet in each restroom; when one is unavailable, service is limited, contributing to the need for a year-round portable toilet. The conversion would provide additional "completely ADA accessible, family accessible" facilities and potentially eliminate that portable toilet. Water and other existing infrastructure already serve the concession area.

The preliminary allowance is $75,000, with staff seeking additional pricing. Staff explained that substantial-improvement restrictions limit spending within a three-year period to 50% of the building's value. A roughly $200,000 building valuation would allow about $100,000, so the proposed amount leaves room for other necessary improvements. Timing is uncertain: staff may advance the project in this budget or defer it because of the department's workload.

6e7b4f6a629857aeb589884cb0bd7d21.Title: Veterans Park Trail Race Timing and Event Services
6e7b4f6a629857aeb589884cb0bd7d21._desc:
Bethany Parks & Recreation is planning a new trail race using Veterans Park and adjoining land trust trails. Mike stated that he would meet with Bob from the land trust the following week to walk a proposed course and determine feasibility. The concept is a four-mile loop, with an eight-mile option consisting of two loops. An initial turnout of 50 to 100 runners would be considered a success, primarily high-school-age participants and adults.

Once the course is mapped, Mike intends to begin contacting timing companies: "I want to get a few quotes" because companies charge different prices per bib. Another commissioner stated, "We should get three quotes anyways with anything." The envisioned service includes chipped race bibs that distinguish one-loop and two-loop participants and record the correct start and finish times. Staff discussed obtaining timing-company referrals from other local races and recreation departments; no supplier was selected.

Related event purchases discussed include participant T-shirts, awards, and portable toilets. Possible awards include medals for age groups and small items such as pint glasses for the top three male and female finishers. Officials also identified aid stations, volunteers, course marking, emergency-service requirements, waivers, marketing, and a race budget as planning needs. The land trust's anticipated role would include providing trail access, helping mark the course, and supplying volunteers to guide runners.

May 16, 2027 was initially proposed, but officials also discussed moving the event to fall 2027, potentially September or October. No date was finalized and no action was taken. Planning will return to the November meeting. The original spring schedule contemplated marketing and registration preparation by January 1, with commission review followed by Board of Selectmen approval, but the schedule may change if the event moves to fall.

8dee7dee60825e58b710ffed670a8de0._desc: The City of Beaverton is seeking a qualified operator to manage the Beaverton Safe Parking Program. Safe Parking offers a legal option for people who are experiencing homelessness and living in a vehicle to park and stay in one of five safe parking locations throughout the city while receiving case management from highly qualified professionals with the goal of transitioning to stable housing. Safe Parking consists of a public-private partnership in which the City contracts out with private organizations who have agreed to offer a limited number of parking places on their properties as designated Safe Parking locations.The Request for Proposals (RFP) will award $58,000 for program case management and an additional $15,000 to be used as flexible funds for other expenses (gas cards, minor vehicle repairs, etc.). The City of Beaverton provides additional funds for program infrastructure (port-a-potties, handwashing stations, and storage pods).Qualified applicants will have a strong ability to work with extremely vulnerable populations through a trauma-informed lens while responsibly working in collaboration with the City of Beaverton (including police), other service providers, host sites, surrounding neighbors, and other key stakeholders.
